_comment: One corpus, read by the fuzz tier, the concurrency drivers and the browser tiers. JSON precisely so both languages read the same bytes: a value that breaks the server through the API and a value that breaks it through the UI should be the same value, and keeping two lists is how they stop being. Every invisible character is written as a \u escape rather than pasted in -- a reviewer has to be able to see what is in the corpus, and a zero-width space pasted literally is indistinguishable from a typo.

strings.why: empty
one space
leading and trailing whitespace, which trim() would hide
a NUL, which Postgres refuses in text outright
a newline, which breaks line-oriented log parsing
a CR/LF pair, the header-injection shape
a tab, which the suite's own TSV plumbing would eat
a DEL byte
astral plane; a LATIN1 cluster refuses it at the server with 22P05
a combining sequence, longer decomposed than composed
right-to-left override, which reverses how a name displays
a zero-width space, invisible in every UI that renders it
a byte-order mark at the front
SQL metacharacters; parameterised queries should make this dull
a script tag, for anything rendered with v-html
an img onerror, which survives naive tag stripping
a template expression, for anything compiled as a Vue template
path traversal, for anything that becomes a filename
an absolute path
a format string, for anything reaching a printf-alike
a shell substitution, for anything reaching a shell
a JSON document as a string value
255 characters -- a common column width, exactly at the edge
256 characters -- one past it
a UUID that is well-formed and matches nothing
a UUID missing a character
the nil UUID, which some code treats as absent
a number in a string, for anything that parses leniently
a value JavaScript and Rust disagree about
a link-local URL, for anything that fetches what it is handed

scalars.why: null where a value is expected
false where a string is expected
true where a string is expected
i64 max, past what a double represents exactly
a float where an integer is expected
an array where a scalar is expected
an object where a scalar is expected

timestamps.why: an offset that is not UTC
a leap day in a leap year
a leap day in a year that has none
the DST spring-forward gap in America/Chicago -- this time does not exist
the autumn fall-back hour, which happens twice
a year past what a date column holds
a plausible date that is not a date
